rundown: Bullets beat Kings 115-104. Bullets led 54-52 at the half and never looked back. The 3rd quarter decided it: Bullets won it 33-23.
Leading the way — Kings: Will Johnston 23 pts, 4 ast; Xavier Cooks 7 reb. Bullets: Max Mackinnon 23 pts; Arnas Velicka 7 ast; Tyrell Harrison 13 reb.
Where Bullets won it: they won the boards 42-31, had 33 assists to 15 and turned it over 7 times to 9.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 22, 12:55 AM ET. It had Kings 81% and Bullets 19%, projecting Kings 101.6 – Bullets 91.3 (192.9 total, Kings by 10.3).

Final: Kings 104 – Bullets 115. Wrong winner: it had Kings at 81%, and Bullets (19%) won.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Kings came in with a 2% above average attack and a 2% stingier than average defense (9-4, 98.6 scored and 89.7 allowed a game over 13 games), worth about 9 and 9 games of evidence. Projected to score 101.6, they scored 104 (+2.4 points, 2% over); projected to allow 91.3, they allowed 115 (+23.7 points, 26% over).

Bullets came in with a 5% below average attack and a 2% leakier than average defense (6-8, 94.4 scored and 99.2 allowed a game over 14 games), worth about 9 and 9 games of evidence. Projected to score 91.3, they scored 115 (+23.7 points, 26% over); projected to allow 101.6, they allowed 104 (+2.4 points, 2% over).

The bigger miss was Bullets' scoring (+23.7 points against projection); both sides outscored their projections, so the game ran hotter than either team's numbers said.

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 219 against 192.9 projected (+26.1), about the 95th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±16).

Margin: Bullets by 11 against Kings by 10.3 projected, about the 96th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±12).

An unusual result, but one the simulations saw regularly (roughly one game in six to one in twenty).

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body: No line was priced for this game (no posted odds, or not enough data to price one).

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: there were no odds to check the projection against.

The projection missed by a lot, so those flags likely mattered here.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×1.157 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +20.1 points. It counts toward Hoops+ scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 103 graded Hoops+ games the algo now scales scoring ×1.020 and gives home teams -1.2 points. Team corrections so far: Kings attack ×1.001, defense ×1.018 (4 games); Bullets attack ×1.013, defense ×1.016 (4 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Wrong side, total outside its normal range, margin outside its normal range (off by 21.3 points), no bet.
